## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*Oguṇṭhita* ("Covering the head") is the twenty-third training rule (*sekhiya*) in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. It establishes monastic etiquette regarding bodily deportment, specifically training monks not to go or sit covered over the head in inhabited areas. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule forms part of a uniform series of decorum rules governing conduct in settlements, displaying extensive formulaic overlap with neighboring and related *sekhiya* training rules [DharmaNexus]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reveals substantial segment sharing across Pali Vinaya texts, particularly with Sekhiya 21, Sekhiya 22, Sekhiya 24, and Sekhiya 5 [DharmaNexus].

*Oguṇṭhita* has extensive parallels across early Buddhist monastic lineages, preserved in Pali, Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan. Curated parallels include the corresponding Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk23*), the Bhikkhu Parivāra, and the Bhikkhunī Vinaya (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk23*, *pli-tv-bi-pm-sk23*). Cross-tradition parallels are attested in the Vinayas and Prātimokṣa sūtras of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions.
